newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends down, gilts soft in light trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends down, gilts soft in light trade.

text.p: Indian call money ended Tuesday easier on improved funds supply while government securities were steady to firm in moderate trade, dealers said.
They said a central bank repurchase of government securities injected 20 billion rupees into banks, improving liquidity and pushing call money rates down.
Dealers said call money ended at 7.0-7.25 percent, off opening quotes of 7.75-8.25 percent and down from Monday's close of 8.0-8.5 percent.
Most of Tuesday's trade was in a 7.5-7.75 percent band, said a dealer at a public sector bank.
"Call money should ease further to around 6.0-7.0 percent by close tomorrow," he said. "There are no major outflows projected for the next few days."
Dealers said government securities were soft but trade was moderate.
"There was some buying interest but prices were soft," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "There was a good deal of interest in treasury bills today and yields fell a bit."
He said trade in bonds was largely in maturities from 2001 to 2005.
Treasury bills maturing in July 1998 yielded 8.25 percent against Monday's 8.35 percent, dealers said.
They said October 1997 bills yielded 7.2 percent.
Among actively traded bonds, the 12.59 percent 2004 fell to 106.80 rupees from 106.95, the 10.85 percent 2001 dropped to 100.5 from 100.64 and the 11.83 percent 2003 ended at 103.56 against 103.65.
